narrative.overview:
A working reference laid open. The verse, its translations, its commentary and the indexes that lead to other verses are all within reach on one surface. The owner's words for the present look are plain, dense and practical: it is a tool for looking things up and comparing, and atmosphere comes second to information.

The surface is paper-coloured with dark ink for text and one deep green-blue for anything that leads somewhere. Everything is set in serif type. There is almost no decoration: boxes are drawn with a single thin line, and the only ornament is a band of keffiyeh pattern across the front page.

The pages that list things are indexes, as at the back of a book: names in columns under headings, a number at the end of each line. Tables with tabs, which the site used until 2026-10-12, are gone.
keyCharacteristics: Paper and ink, in a light theme and a dark theme with the same roles.
One colour for links at rest, a second for hover and focus.
Serif type throughout, with dedicated faces for Arabic and Urdu.
Thin lines, rounded corners, almost no shadow.
Indexes in columns, not tables: a name, and its count at the end of the row.
Three columns on a wide screen (menu, page, and a rail of contents and backlinks); the listing pages and a theme's page give the rail's width to the page.

rules.name: The Two Greens Rule
rules.body: Ink Teal means "this leads somewhere". Olive Leaf means "you are pointing at this". Neither is used for the other's job, and plugin controls are brought into line with it.

rules.name: The You Are Here Rule
rules.body: The page being read (in the menu, in a theme's surah index) is marked by weight 600 and an Ink Teal Wash, and says so to a screen reader. A selected arrangement is filled with Ink Teal. Neither uses Olive Leaf, and neither relies on colour alone.

rules.name: The Readable Small Text Rule
rules.body: Text under 1rem is never set in Faded Ink. It uses Faded Ink Strong or darker.

rules.name: The Marked Language Rule
rules.body: Arabic and Urdu text is tagged with its language so that it gets its own face, its own line spacing and right-to-left direction. Latin text never borrows those settings and they never borrow Latin ones. Where the generator knows the language it says so in the note; the site guesses only what is left.

dos: Do use Ink Teal for links at rest and Olive Leaf for hover, pressed and the focus ring, including on controls a plugin draws.
Do mark the page being read with weight and an Ink Teal Wash, and a selected control with an Ink Teal fill.
Do set small secondary text in Faded Ink Strong, and outline a control in Faded Ink.
Do mark Arabic and Urdu text with its language so it gets its own face.
Do keep anything a finger must hit at least 2.75rem tall.
Do list things as an index (names in columns, count at the end of the row), with a filter and arrangements where the list is long.
Do use `dvh`, never `vh`, for anything that fills a phone screen.
donts: Don't treat these present faults as part of the system. They are recorded so they are not copied: hovered text in Olive Leaf is 3.2:1 on the dark page; the feedback button floats over the page's content; the phone's bar loses the site's name when the text size is doubled; tag chips on an ayah's page show a theme's key and not its name.
Don't bring back a table with tabs for a list of entries. Three of them were replaced by indexes in October 2026, after being 7 to 16 screens long.
Don't read the Elevation and Components sections as rules. The owner left both undecided.
Don't treat any of this as binding identity. All of it is open to change with the owner's approval.
